parts.text:
26 Orange light in a vacuum has a wavelength of 600 nm.
What is the frequency of this light?
A
180 Hz
B
5.0 × 105
Hz
C
1.8 × 1011
Hz
D
5.0 × 1014
Hz

hints: Notice the light travels in a vacuum, so its speed is $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and the wavelength is $600 \text{ nm}$.
Recall the wave equation $c = f\lambda$ for electromagnetic waves and convert $600 \text{ nm}$ to $6.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Rearrange to $f = c/\lambda$ and check the power of ten when dividing $10^8$ by $10^{-7}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $\lambda = 600 \text{ nm}$ in a vacuum, so wave speed $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Convert wavelength to SI units: $1 \text{ nm} = 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, so $\lambda = 600 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m} = 6.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
State the governing relation for all progressive waves: $v = f\lambda$, which for light in vacuum is $c = f\lambda$.
Substitute with units: $f = (3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1})/(6.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}) = 0.50 \times 10^{15} \text{ Hz} = 5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.

A.explanation: 180 Hz comes from multiplying $600$ by $0.3$ without converting nm to m or using $3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ correctly.

B.explanation: This value results if $600 \text{ nm}$ is taken as $600 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ instead of $600 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: This value results from multiplying $c$ by $\lambda$ instead of dividing $c$ by $\lambda$.
